blocks.text: At Bag Factory Artists’ Studios in Johannesburg, ‘Site Forming: Where Encounter Takes Form’ brings together the practices of two emerging artists to examine memory, identity and the transformative possibilities of space.

How do the places we inhabit shape who we become? In ‘Site Forming: Where Encounter Takes Form’, artists Swaline Mkhonto and Zovuyo Pendu investigate the shifting relationships between bodies, memories, environments and inner worlds.

Presented at Bag Factory Artists’ Studios, the exhibition marks the culmination of their participation in the 2025/2026 Young Womxn Studio Bursary Award. Mkhonto’s interdisciplinary practice draws on printmaking, installation, writing and mark-making to explore fragmentation, memory and the body’s relationship with space. Pendu’s figurative paintings investigate the psychological tensions between faith, ego and the unconscious, questioning how identity is shaped through personal experience. Together, their practices approach the idea of a site as something continually transformed through encounter rather than a fixed location.

The exhibition includes curatorial contributions from Penina Chalumbira and collaboration with Letsema collective members Ntabiseng Mofokeng, Mbako Moemise and Eva Rose London. Supported by Sam Nhlengethwa, Bag Factory Artists’ Studios and the National Arts Council, the exhibition reflects the bursary’s commitment to nurturing emerging womxn artists and encouraging experimentation within Johannesburg’s contemporary art landscape.
This exhibition is on view at Bag Factory Artists’ Studios in Newtown, Johannesburg, until 6 November 2026.
